claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, their eligibility for Child Benefit depends on their current situation. Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in one of the following:

1. In full-time approved education (such as A-levels, T-levels, or equivalent qualifications at school or college - but not university/higher education)
2. On an approved training course (such as a government-funded training programme)
3. Neither of the above

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is still in college doing A-levels, so yes, they're in full-time education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that Alex is in full-time education doing A-levels. That's helpful information.

Now I have a couple more questions to assess your eligibility:

Are you responsible for Alex, meaning do they live with you, or do you contribute financially towards their upbringing at least equal to the amount of Child Benefit?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's good to know.

I have one more important question regarding your circumstances:

Do you live in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:
- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex lives with you
- Alex is in full-time approved education (doing A-levels at college)

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. The rules state that you normally qualify if your child is under 20 and stays in approved education or training (which includes A-levels), and you are responsible for them (Alex lives with you).

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why you qualify:

- ✅ **You live in the UK** (Manchester)
- ✅ **You are responsible for Alex** (they live with you)
- ✅ **Alex is in approved education** – A-levels at college counts as approved full-time education
- ✅ **Alex is under 20** – Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 as long as they remain in approved education or training

**Important things to note:**
- You'll continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex as long as they stay in approved education or training and are under 20
- Eligibility would stop if Alex starts paid work for 24 hours or more per week while no longer in approved education, starts an apprenticeship in England, or starts receiving certain benefits like Universal Credit in their own right

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
